newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary blocks WTO panel on export subsidy row.
newsitem.headline: Hungary blocks WTO panel on export subsidy row.

text.p: Hungary on Wednesday blocked a four-country bid for the creation of a World Trade Organisation panel to rule on Hungary's breaking of the WTO's agricultural export subsidies ceiling.
"We think that there is still room for negotiations," Laszlo Varkonyi, head of the Trade and Industry Ministry's International Organisations Department, told a news conference.
Argentina, Australia, New Zealand and the United States have accused Hungary of breaching agricultural export subsidy curbs approved at the 1992 Uruguay GATT talks.
Hungary claims that the limits imposed are based on wrong export subsidy figures for the period between 1986 and 1990 supplied by the then communist Hungarian government.
In Uruguay Hungary reported export subsidies of 22 billion forints ($130 million) instead of the actual 58 billion and is expected to reduce this to 14.32 billion by the year 2000.
Hungary would like 1995 to be used as the base year and to register the subsidy figures in dollars instead of forints because of high inflation, currently around 24 percent.
In 1995 Hungary spent some $350 million on agricultural export subsidies, down from the annual average of $1 billion between 1986 and 1990, Varkonyi said.
He added that the four plaintiff countries are more afraid of Hungary setting a precedent by going back on an 1992 agreement than of the threat Hungarian exports actually pose.
"The difficulty is that this is a matter of principle, not an everyday dispute where the sides can meet halfway," Varkonyi said.

The four countries brought the case to the WTO's Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) but Hungary rejected the proposal to set up a panel saying it still hopes a negotiated solution before the next meeting of the DSB on February 25.
Varkonyi added that further talks would be held in Geneva but Hungary has not yet asked for a meeting.
"We earlier sent them a proposal which they did not answer," he said. "To some extent, the ball is in their court now".
If agreement cannot be reached by February 25, a DSB panel will automatically be set up. ($1=169.06 Forint)
